settings.text:
Double-glazed glass production machinery is particularly useful today, as air and noise pollution continue to increase. In large, densely populated cities, noise pollution has become a major concern, and insulated double-glazed glass helps prevent outside noise from entering indoor spaces.
Double-glazed glass also offers many other benefits, which is why it has become so widely used. Many glass manufacturing plants across the country now operate double-glazed glass production lines and use professional, up-to-date machinery for this purpose.
In this article, we will first provide a brief overview of double-glazed glass and its different types, and then introduce the machinery used to manufacture it. Read on to learn more.

settings.title: Facts About Double-Glazed Glass
settings.text:
In recent years, double-glazed glass has become widely used as an effective solution for reducing noise and environmental pollution inside buildings.
These glass units are manufactured by filling the space between the two panes with an inert gas such as argon or, alternatively, with dry air.
This helps reduce the transfer of heat and cold through the glass, minimizing energy loss in both winter and summer. It also significantly reduces sound transmission.
Installing double-glazed glass in a building is estimated to save an average of approximately 40 cubic meters of natural gas per year.
Given its significant role in reducing noise pollution, double-glazed glass is also estimated to reduce sound transmission by approximately 30 decibels.
Today, many types of double-glazed glass are manufactured in different shapes and colors and can be installed in custom dimensions.
In modern buildings, very large double-glazed windows are often installed, providing effective insulation while adding exceptional visual appeal.

settings.title: Types of Double-Glazed Glass
settings.text:
Double-glazed glass consists of two panes positioned parallel to each other to improve the overall performance of the glazing unit.
These glass panes are manufactured and used in various thicknesses, including 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 mm.
Double-glazed glass is not a specific type of glass in itself. Different types of glass available on the market can be used to manufacture insulated glazing units.
Common types used in double-glazed units include:
Float Glass (Clear Glass)
This is glass used in double-glazed units in the same condition in which it comes out of the furnace. It has not undergone additional processing to improve its properties and is less resistant than other types of glass.
Tempered Glass
This special type of glass undergoes rapid heating to a high temperature followed by rapid cooling, making it highly resistant to pressure, impact, and temperature changes.
Sandblasted Glass
Another widely used type of glass for double-glazed units is sandblasted glass. During production, patterns are created on the glass surface using sand and water, giving it an attractive, frosted appearance.
Laminated Glass
This type is made by combining two strong glass panes with a gel-like interlayer between them. If the glass breaks, the fragments remain attached to this interlayer, preventing them from scattering.
Reflective Glass
This type of glass can be seen in many building windows. Its distinctive feature is its mirror-like surface, achieved by applying metallic coatings that make the glass reflective.
Patterned Glass
This type of glass features distinctive embossed or textured patterns.

settings.title: Double-Glazed Glass Production Machinery
settings.text:
Now that you are familiar with the features of double-glazed glass, it is useful to learn more about how it is manufactured.
At the factory, the glass panes are first cut and then washed using treated water. Special spacer frames are subsequently prepared for the glass units.
The inner cavity of each spacer frame is then filled with a moisture-absorbing desiccant, and the frame is thoroughly sealed.
After the glass panes are assembled with the spacer frame, the cavity between them is filled with argon gas. Finally, polysulfide sealant is applied to seal the unit.
Because this process requires a high degree of precision, all the stages mentioned above are performed automatically using the following machinery:
